tool.kick.countMovements: Count fetal movements during an active session. What matters most is learning your own baby's usual pattern and telling your team when it changes. Formal counting on its own has not been shown to reduce stillbirth, so treat this as a way to learn that pattern rather than a test to pass. A drop in movement is worth a call whatever this counter says.
tool.common.timeToGoToThe: 🚨 Time to go to the hospital
tool.feed.fewFeedsBody: Newborns typically need 8–12 feedings per 24 hours. If baby is difficult to wake or not gaining weight, call your doctor.
tool.diaper.day1212: Day 1–2: 1–2 wet diapers · Day 3–4: 3–4 wet · Day 5+: 6+ wet, 3–4 dirty per day. Fewer than 6 wet diapers after day 5 → call your doctor.
tool.jaundice.setBirthDateHint: Set baby's birth date above to see day-by-day guidance.
tool.jaundice.day1: First day. Bilirubin is being checked before hospital discharge. Baby is monitored by the nursing staff.
tool.jaundice.day2: Bilirubin levels are rising. Hospital checks before discharge. Watch for yellowing of skin and whites of eyes.
tool.jaundice.day3: Jaundice peaks around days 3–5 in most babies. Yellow color may be more visible. Feeding frequently (8–12 times/day) helps the body clear bilirubin.
tool.jaundice.day4: Peak jaundice period. Make sure baby is feeding well and having wet diapers. Pediatrician visit may be scheduled around now.
tool.jaundice.day5: Pediatrician visit: weight check + bilirubin level. Levels should start to level off. If baby is sleepy and not feeding, call your doctor.
tool.jaundice.day6: Levels should start declining in full-term babies. Continue feeding frequently. If skin is deeply yellow or baby won't wake to feed. Call your doctor.
tool.jaundice.day7: Most term babies' jaundice is improving by now. Watch for yellowing spreading to legs and feet, which signals higher levels.
tool.jaundice.day10: In most term babies, jaundice is nearly resolved. If it's persisting or worsening, your doctor will want to check a bilirubin level.
tool.jaundice.day14: 2-week visit. Jaundice should be resolved in term babies. Persistent jaundice beyond 2 weeks may need further evaluation. Tell your doctor.
tool.jaundice.day21: Jaundice lasting beyond 3 weeks is considered prolonged and should be evaluated. Breastfed babies can have mild jaundice longer, but it still needs to be checked.
tool.jaundice.redFlags: Baby won't wake to feed · Deeply yellow skin spreading to legs · Arching back or high-pitched cry · White or grey stools · Very dark urine
tool.bp.anyReading14090During: Any reading ≥ 140/90 during pregnancy or postpartum. ≥ 160/110 is a medical emergency. Call L&D or 911.

tool.nausea.intro: Nausea is usually worse on an empty stomach, so small amounts often beat big meals. Tap each hour you ate or drank something. The point is not how much, it is how long the gaps are.
tool.nausea.tapHour: Tap an hour to mark that you ate
tool.nausea.gapOk: {hours} hours. Try to keep gaps under about 3 hours while you are awake.
tool.nausea.gapLong: {hours} hours. Long gaps make nausea worse. Try something small, even a few bites.
tool.nausea.weekPrompt: Enter the week of pregnancy you are in, so this can show you where you are.
tool.nausea.timelineLabel: Nausea timeline, you are at week {week}
tool.nausea.phaseEarly: Nausea often begins around week 6. If it has not started, it may not start at all.
tool.nausea.phasePeak: This is usually the hardest stretch. It tends to peak around weeks 9 to 10 and then ease.
tool.nausea.phaseEasing: For most women it starts easing from here. About 6 in 10 are past it by week 14.
tool.nausea.phaseMost: About 9 in 10 women are past the worst by week 22. If yours is not easing, tell your doctor.
tool.nausea.phaseLate: Nausea this late is less common. It is worth telling your doctor, who can look for other causes.
tool.nausea.flag.noFluids: You cannot keep any fluids down for a whole day
tool.nausea.flag.vomitingOften: You are vomiting several times a day, every day
tool.nausea.flag.weightLoss: You are losing weight instead of gaining
tool.nausea.flag.darkUrine: Your urine is dark, or you have not passed any for 8 hours
tool.nausea.flag.dizzy: You feel dizzy or faint when you stand up
tool.nausea.callTodayBody: Severe pregnancy sickness has a name, hyperemesis gravidarum, and it is treatable. The real danger is dehydration, not the nausea itself. Do not wait it out.
tool.nausea.strat.empty.name: Never let your stomach get empty
tool.nausea.strat.empty.how: Eat something small before you get hungry, and keep crackers by the bed for before you sit up.
tool.nausea.strat.bland.name: Bland, dry, cold food
tool.nausea.strat.bland.how: Cold food smells less. Dry toast, crackers, plain rice, cold fruit.
tool.nausea.strat.fluids.name: Sip fluids between meals
tool.nausea.strat.fluids.how: Drinking with food fills you up faster. Sip small amounts all day instead.
tool.nausea.strat.triggers.name: Learn your triggers
tool.nausea.strat.triggers.how: Smells are the usual culprit. Cooking, coffee, perfume. Let someone else cook if you can.
tool.nausea.strat.b6.name: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine)
tool.nausea.strat.b6.how: 10 to 25 mg, three or four times a day. No more than 200 mg in 24 hours. Sold over the counter.
tool.nausea.strat.ginger.name: Ginger
tool.nausea.strat.ginger.how: Tea, capsules, or chews. Modest evidence, and it helps some women a lot.
tool.nausea.strat.acupressure.name: Wrist pressure
tool.nausea.strat.acupressure.how: Pressing the P6 point, or a wristband. See the instructions below.
tool.nausea.strat.vitamin.name: Move your prenatal vitamin
tool.nausea.strat.vitamin.how: Iron is a common culprit. Take it at night, or with food. Ask about a low-iron option.
tool.nausea.strat.rest.name: Rest, and get up slowly
tool.nausea.strat.rest.how: Tiredness makes nausea worse. Sit on the edge of the bed a moment before standing.
tool.nausea.strat.doxylamine.name: Doxylamine, added to B6
tool.nausea.strat.doxylamine.how: 12.5 mg at bedtime, which is half a 25 mg Unisom SleepTab. If that is not enough your doctor may add a morning and afternoon dose. No more than 50 mg in 24 hours. Buy SleepTabs, not SleepGels: SleepGels are a different drug. No prescription needed.
tool.nausea.triedAll: You have marked everything as tried. If nothing is helping, that is worth a call.
tool.nausea.stratNote: Tap anything you have tried to keep track. Ask your doctor before starting a supplement or medicine.
tool.nausea.howIsItNow: How is the nausea right now?
tool.nausea.lowerIsBetter: Lower is better. This is only your own record, not medical proof.
tool.nausea.noEntries: No entries yet. Log how you feel a few times and this will show what helps you.
tool.nausea.acuIntro: Evidence is mixed, but it costs nothing, has no side effects, and helps some women. Worth ten minutes to find out.
tool.nausea.acuBands: Elastic wristbands with a plastic stud, sold for travel sickness, press the same point. Wear one on each wrist.
tool.nausea.acu.find: Turn one hand palm up, fingers relaxed.
tool.nausea.acu.measure: Lay three fingers of your other hand across the wrist, with the finger nearest your hand sitting on the crease where your hand meets your arm.
tool.nausea.acu.feel: The point is just past your third finger, in the middle of the wrist. Press around and you should feel two firm cords running down the arm. The point sits between them.
tool.nausea.acu.press: Press firmly with your thumb, hard enough to feel it but not to hurt. Small circles or steady pressure, for two to three minutes.
tool.nausea.acu.both: Do the same on the other wrist. Repeat whenever the nausea rises.
tool.nausea.logIntro: Rate the nausea whenever it changes. After a few entries this will show which of the things you tried actually helped you.

usNotice.title: Care in the United States
usNotice.body: This guide describes prenatal care as it is provided in the United States, and is written for mothers receiving their care here. Prenatal care differs a great deal between countries. Visit schedules, tests and recommendations elsewhere may not match what you read here. If you are receiving care in another country, this app probably isn’t for you.
